questions.q: A 35-year-old male from rural Maharashtra presents with a hypopigmented patch on the forearm with loss of sensation. Slit skin smear shows acid-fast bacilli. Nerve biopsy reveals granulomatous infiltration with foamy macrophages and no lymphocytes. What type of leprosy is this?
questions.exp: Foamy macrophages (Virchow cells) packed with bacilli, sparse lymphocytes, and high bacterial load on SSS are hallmarks of lepromatous leprosy. The cell-mediated immunity is deficient, allowing unrestricted bacillary multiplication.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman develops a sudden erythematous eruption on the face and trunk with flaccid blisters that rupture easily, leaving raw erosions. Nikolsky's sign is positive. Immunofluorescence shows intercellular IgG deposition in a 'chicken wire' pattern. The most appropriate first-line treatment is:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris with positive Nikolsky's sign and intercellular IgG (anti-desmoglein antibodies) requires systemic corticosteroids as first-line therapy. Prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day is the standard starting dose.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic male presents with a rapidly spreading painful cellulitis on the leg with crepitus on palpation. X-ray shows gas in soft tissues. The most likely causative organism is:
questions.exp: Gas gangrene (clostridial myonecrosis) caused by Clostridium perfringens is characterised by gas in tissues (crepitus), rapidly spreading necrosis, and a sweet-smelling discharge. Occurs commonly in diabetics and immunocompromised patients.

questions.q: A 22-year-old male presents with painless chancre on the glans penis. Dark-field microscopy of the exudate shows spiral organisms with corkscrew motility. The treatment of choice is:
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis caused by Treponema pallidum is treated with Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM as a single dose. This is the drug of choice per WHO and national guidelines.

questions.q: A 30-year-old HIV-positive patient presents with painful grouped vesicles on an erythematous base along the T5 dermatome. The diagnosis is herpes zoster. The most appropriate antiviral regimen in this immunocompromised patient is:
questions.exp: In immunocompromised patients with herpes zoster, IV Acyclovir is preferred to prevent dissemination and visceral involvement. Oral antivirals are reserved for immunocompetent patients.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with scaly, well-defined erythematous plaques with silvery scales on the elbows, knees, and scalp. Auspitz sign is positive. Histopathology shows Munro microabscesses. The pathognomonic finding in psoriasis is:
questions.exp: Munro microabscesses (neutrophil collections in the stratum corneum) are pathognomonic of psoriasis. Kogoj's spongiform pustules are seen in pustular psoriasis. All other findings are characteristic but not pathognomonic.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male presents with tense bullae on erythematous skin. Immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 deposition at the dermoepidermal junction. Electron microscopy would show deposits in:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid has deposits within the lamina lucida (between lamina lucida and basal cells), targeting BP180 (type XVII collagen) and BP230. This distinguishes it from EBA (below lamina densa) and dermatitis herpetiformis.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman on long-term chloroquine for discoid lupus presents with bilateral painless visual field loss. The most likely explanation is:
questions.exp: Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine can cause irreversible retinopathy with 'bull's eye' maculopathy, leading to paracentral scotomas. Regular ophthalmological screening is mandatory. Corneal deposits also occur but are reversible.

questions.q: A 20-year-old student presents with annular, scaly patches on the scalp with broken hair shafts (black dots). KOH examination shows arthroconidia within hair shafts. This pattern is characteristic of:
questions.exp: Black dot tinea capitis is caused by endothrix dermatophytes (T. tonsurans, T. violaceum) where hyphae and arthroconidia fill the entire hair shaft, causing it to break at the scalp surface leaving black dots.

questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with hypopigmented macules on the trunk with fine scaling. Wood's lamp shows golden-yellow fluorescence. KOH shows 'spaghetti and meatballs' pattern. Treatment of choice for localised disease is:
opts: Oral fluconazole 150 mg weekly for 4 weeks
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor caused by Malassezia furfur shows spaghetti and meatball (hyphae + yeast) on KOH. Topical antifungals (ketoconazole shampoo, selenium sulfide) are first-line for localised disease.

questions.q: A 50-year-old male presents with noduloulcerative lesion on the lower lip that has been slowly enlarging over 2 years. Biopsy shows islands of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and stromal retraction. The most appropriate treatment is:
opts: Wide local excision with 4 mm margin
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma at a high-risk site (lower lip) with potential for significant cosmetic morbidity is best treated with Mohs micrographic surgery, offering the highest cure rate with maximal tissue conservation.

questions.q: A 65-year-old male farmer presents with a hyperkeratotic plaque on the dorsum of the hand with central ulceration. Biopsy shows dysplastic keratinocytes extending through the full thickness of the epidermis with dermal invasion and keratin pearls. Diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Full-thickness epidermal dysplasia with dermal invasion and keratin pearl formation is diagnostic of invasive squamous cell carcinoma. Bowen's disease shows full-thickness dysplasia WITHOUT invasion. Keratin pearls (horn pearls) indicate squamous differentiation.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with comedones, papules, and pustules on the face. The most important pathogenic factor in acne is:
opts: Sebaceous gland hyperactivity under androgen influence
questions.exp: The initial event in acne pathogenesis is follicular hyperkeratinisation leading to microcomedo formation. This precedes sebum accumulation, P. acnes colonisation, and subsequent inflammation. All factors contribute but microcomedo is the initiating lesion.

questions.q: A 30-year-old female on isotretinoin for severe nodular acne is found to be pregnant at 6 weeks. The most significant risk of isotretinoin teratogenicity is:
questions.exp: Isotretinoin is a potent teratogen causing retinoid embryopathy: craniofacial malformations (microtia, anotia, cleft palate), cardiac defects, CNS abnormalities, and thymic aplasia. Craniofacial defects are most characteristic.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with malar rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, and joint pain. ANA is positive (1:640, homogeneous). Anti-dsDNA antibodies are positive. The skin biopsy of the malar rash would most likely show:
opts: Interface dermatitis with basal layer vacuolation and dermal mucin
questions.exp: SLE shows interface dermatitis with vacuolar degeneration of basal keratinocytes, dermal mucin deposition, and perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate. DIF shows 'lupus band' (IgG, IgM, C3) at the DEJ in lesional skin.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male presents with Raynaud's phenomenon, skin tightening involving the fingers, hands, and face, and difficulty swallowing. Anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) antibodies are positive. This pattern is consistent with:
questions.exp: Anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) is associated with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis with proximal skin involvement and high risk of pulmonary fibrosis. Anti-centromere antibodies are associated with limited SSc/CREST.

questions.q: A 20-year-old male presents with recurrent painful oral ulcers, genital ulcers, and uveitis. Pathergy test is positive. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: The triad of recurrent oral ulcers, genital ulcers, and uveitis along with a positive pathergy test (sterile pustule at needlestick site within 48h) is diagnostic of Behçet's disease.

questions.q: A 55-year-old HIV-positive male presents with violaceous nodules on the skin and mucosa. Biopsy shows spindle cells, extravasated red blood cells, and slit-like vascular spaces. HHV-8 is implicated. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Kaposi's sarcoma in HIV patients (AIDS-KS, epidemic type) is caused by HHV-8. Biopsy shows proliferating spindle cells forming slit-like vascular channels with extravasated RBCs. Bacillary angiomatosis (Bartonella) can mimic KS clinically.

questions.q: A 30-year-old male presents with grouped vesicles on the genitalia with painful inguinal lymphadenopathy. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. The first episode treatment is:
questions.exp: First episode genital herpes (HSV-2) is treated with Acyclovir 400 mg TDS for 7-10 days (or 200 mg 5x/day). Longer duration is used for the first episode compared to recurrences to reduce severity and duration.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male presents with painless papular lesions on the penis with umbilication. Giemsa staining of the expressed content shows Henderson-Patterson bodies. The causative agent is:
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum is caused by Molluscum contagiosum virus (a poxvirus). Henderson-Patterson bodies are large intracytoplasmic inclusions visible on Giemsa staining. Umbilicated papules are characteristic.

questions.q: A 60-year-old male presents with an erythematous scaly plaque on the chest with central clearing and a 'herald patch' that appeared 2 weeks ago. Christmas tree distribution on the back. The causative agent is:
questions.exp: Pityriasis rosea is associated with HHV-6 and HHV-7 reactivation. It begins with a herald patch, followed by Christmas tree distribution along Langer's lines on the trunk. Spontaneous resolution in 6-8 weeks.

questions.q: A 45-year-old female presents with a well-defined hyperpigmented patch on the face aggravated by sun exposure. Wood's lamp examination accentuates the pigmentation (enhanced contrast). This is consistent with:
questions.exp: Wood's lamp examination accentuates epidermal pigmentation (melanin in epidermis absorbs UV). Dermal melasma does NOT accentuate under Wood's lamp. This is clinically important for predicting treatment response (epidermal responds better).

questions.q: A 30-year-old male presents with pruritis ani with nocturnal worsening. Cellophane tape test shows eggs. Scotch tape test at anal margin reveals ova. Treatment of choice is:
questions.exp: Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm/threadworm) causing perianal pruritus is diagnosed by Scotch tape test. Albendazole 400 mg single dose (or mebendazole 100 mg single dose) is first-line; repeat after 2 weeks to treat reinfection.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male presents with recurrent blistering on the dorsum of hands after minor trauma, healing with milia and scarring. DIF of perilesional skin shows IgG below the lamina densa. ELISA is positive for type VII collagen antibodies. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: EBA (Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita) is an autoimmune subepidermal blistering disease with antibodies against type VII collagen (anchoring fibrils). IgG deposits below the lamina densa on DIF/EM, with mechanobullous presentation.

questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with extremely pruritic vesicles on elbows, knees, buttocks, and scalp. DIF shows granular IgA deposits at dermal papillary tips. Associated with:
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (Duhring's disease) is pathognomonic for gluten-sensitive enteropathy. Granular IgA at dermal papillary tips on DIF is pathognomonic. Treatment is dapsone + gluten-free diet.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male on carbamazepine presents with fever, confluent erythema involving >30% BSA, positive Nikolsky's sign, and widespread sheet-like skin detachment involving mucous membranes. Mortality risk is approximately:
questions.exp: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN, >30% BSA involvement) is a severe drug reaction with mortality 25-35%. SCORTEN score is used to predict mortality. Carbamazepine, phenytoin, sulfonamides, and allopurinol are common culprits.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male presents with well-demarcated hypopigmented patches with loss of sensation. Lepromin test is strongly positive. Histopathology shows well-formed epithelioid granulomas with rare AFB. This is:
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) has strong cell-mediated immunity reflected by strongly positive lepromin test. Histology shows well-formed epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells, few or absent AFB, and nerve damage.

questions.q: A 30-year-old with leprosy develops sudden onset of painful, tender, erythematous nodules on the face and extremities with fever and malaise. This is diagnosed as ENL (Erythema Nodosum Leprosum). This reaction is seen in which type:
questions.exp: ENL (Type 2 lepra reaction) is an immune complex (Type III hypersensitivity) mediated reaction occurring in LL and BL (lepromatous spectrum) patients. High antigen load triggers immune complex deposition. Treatment is thalidomide or prednisolone.

questions.q: A patient with diffuse scalp alopecia undergoes trichoscopy. The examiner notes 'exclamation mark hairs', yellow dots, and cadaver hairs. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Exclamation mark hairs (tapering proximally, broader distally), yellow dots (dilated follicular openings with sebum/keratin), and black dots (broken hair at scalp) are dermoscopic hallmarks of alopecia areata.

questions.q: A 20-year-old female presents with intense pruritic eruption after wearing new jewellery. Patch testing shows positive reaction to nickel sulfate at 48 and 96 hours. The immunological mechanism is:
questions.exp: Allergic contact dermatitis is a classic Type IV (delayed-type) hypersensitivity reaction mediated by sensitised CD4+ T cells (specifically Th1). Sensitisation phase requires 10-14 days; elicitation begins 48-72 hours after re-exposure.
